description: Three first-in first-out queues written and read by triggers, each holding up to 128 values, so a run of voltages can be stored and played back in the order it arrived

inputs.text: A trigger above 1V stores the voltage at each of the three In jacks as one more entry, and is ignored once 128 entries are held
A trigger above 1V takes the oldest entry out of each queue and holds it at the Out jacks; on an empty queue nothing is read and no trigger is sent
Above 0V, every entry read out is written back onto the end of the queue, so the stored run repeats
A trigger above 1V empties all three queues
The voltage stored in its own queue each time a write trigger arrives, and returned at the matching Out jack

outputs.text: A 10V trigger 1ms long each time an entry is actually read out
Carries 10V while the queues are empty and 0V while they hold anything
The entry read out of its own queue, held until the next read trigger

notes: the figure printed on the panel counts the entries now held, out of a maximum of 128, and the lamp column shows the same count as a bar
The Out jacks rest at 0V until a write trigger has stored something and a read trigger has taken it out; a read on an empty queue does nothing at all
